cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Business websites dominate Gemini's local AI citations — but results shift dramatically by search
stories.plain: Nearly 60% of Gemini's local recommendations link back to business websites, not directories — good news for direct web presence. But the same search query can return wildly different citations, raising serious questions about GEO consistency. Marketers now have data suggesting where to focus optimization effort to stay visible inside AI-generated answers.

stories.head: How to tell if your personalization is over the line
stories.plain: A practical three-part test — does the customer expect it, find it relevant, and feel comfortable with it — gives marketers a governance framework for deciding when 1:1 personalization crosses into creepiness. As AI makes hyper-targeting easier, this kind of ethical guardrail is increasingly important for brand trust and regulatory safety.

stories.head: Iterable CMO on AI-powered real-time decisioning and building customer trust
stories.plain: Iterable's CMO Priya Gill details how brands are using real-time AI decisioning inside customer engagement platforms — choosing the right message, channel, and moment per individual. She also addresses the trust gap: automation gains only hold if customers believe brands are using their data responsibly. Relevant for anyone buying or building a CEP.

stories.head: Seismic-Highspot merger and the week's AI-powered martech releases
stories.plain: The Seismic and Highspot merger creates a dominant GTM enablement platform, but editors flag that disconnected customer data could blunt its value. The round-up also covers agentic add-ons across several martech categories. Important for buyers evaluating consolidation risk in the sales-enablement and AI-content stack.

stories.head: Capacity adds multi-agent support and automated QA to voice AI offerings
stories.plain: Capacity's platform now lets multiple AI agents hand off voice interactions across departments while sharing a single knowledge layer — and it auto-checks call quality without human review. This shows how agentic architectures are moving from chat into voice CX, shifting what brands need to govern and what vendors they need to evaluate.

stories.head: IAB updates standard for disclosing AI in ads
stories.plain: The IAB has revised its framework for when AI use in advertising must be disclosed to consumers. The new line is drawn around content that changes perceptions of authenticity, identity, or what is real. This matters because it sets the compliance baseline that every brand using generative AI in creative will now be measured against.

stories.head: AI visibility index shows which brands are disappearing from AI answers
stories.plain: New index data reveals a sharp split between brands that rank well on Google and those that actually surface inside AI-generated answers. Traditional SEO authority does not reliably predict AI recall, meaning brands with strong search rankings can still be invisible to users asking AI assistants — a fundamental shift in how discoverability is measured.

stories.head: Getting your brand ready for AI agent discovery
stories.plain: Being cited in an AI answer is not enough — the piece explains what determines whether an AI agent actually selects and recommends your brand versus just mentioning it. Practical guidance on structured data, authority signals, and content format makes this directly actionable for marketing and SEO teams adjusting strategy now.

stories.head: How to tell if your personalization is over the line
stories.plain: A practical decision framework for marketers: before deploying customer data for personalization, check whether consumers expect it, find it relevant, and feel comfortable with it. As AI enables ever-finer targeting, this three-part test gives teams a concrete governance tool to avoid the creepiness that erodes trust and triggers regulation.

stories.head: How to stop overpaying for AI complexity
stories.plain: Rule-based, predictive, generative, and agentic AI come with very different cost and risk profiles. The article argues teams should start with the lightest approach that solves the problem and only escalate complexity when simpler methods fail — a buying and architecture principle that directly affects how martech stacks are evaluated and funded.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: Brands Are Invisible to AI Unless They Rebuild for Agent Discovery
body: A new AI visibility index reveals that brands optimized for search engines are quietly vanishing from AI-generated answers — Gemini, for instance, heavily favors direct business websites over aggregators. Winning in AI-mediated discovery requires a fundamentally different content and citation strategy, not just SEO tweaks.

Georgia-Pacific's Jason Ippen frames this as brand stewardship turned offensive: marketers must engineer structured, authoritative signals so AI agents surface them at the moment of consideration. The window to act is narrow — brands that delay cede ground that compounding AI training cycles make increasingly hard to recover.
ev: MarTech · Brand Ready for Agent Discovery

themes.head: The Agentic Stack Matures: Multi-Agent Pipelines Enter Production
body: Multiple vendors this month shipped production-grade multi-agent capabilities — Capacity added automated QA & knowledge orchestration across voice agents, Tricentis pushed agentic software development, and Salesforce's AgentExchange welcomed Agiloft's contract intelligence. This signals a transition from single-purpose AI tools to coordinated agent networks that hand work between specialized models.

Luma's Prince Boucher captures the strategic implication: AI must be built as a core organizational capability, not a series of pilots. Companies still running isolated proof-of-concepts will find it structurally difficult to bolt on the orchestration layer that multi-agent production demands.
ev: Agile Brand · Luma AI as Core Capability

themes.head: Data Architecture Debt Is Now an AI Blocker
body: Commentators this month drew a direct line between legacy data infrastructure and stalled AI ROI: pipelines designed for batch analytics cannot feed real-time agent workflows. Intent data, buyer signals, and CX metrics need to flow instantly into go-to-market systems — exactly what the Intentsify-Clay integration and Liferay Data Platform launch are trying to address.

The CustomerGauge report on the 'CX Monetization Paradox' adds a business consequence: operations are advancing but organizations can't prove value because the underlying data is fragmented. Fixing architecture is no longer an IT backlog item — it is a prerequisite for justifying the AI spend already on the books.
ev: MarTech Series · Intentsify & Clay GTM Workflows

themes.head: Personalization Hits a Trust & Disclosure Reckoning
body: Two forces converged this month: the IAB updated its standard for disclosing AI in ads, and MarTech published explicit guidance on when personalization crosses into consumer discomfort. Regulators and industry bodies are no longer waiting for consensus — disclosure norms are being codified now, meaning marketers who haven't audited their AI-driven targeting face near-term compliance exposure.

The Iterable CMO interview reinforces the tension: AI-powered engagement lifts conversion metrics, but trust erosion from perceived surveillance can quietly hollow out lifetime value. The decision is no longer whether to personalize with AI, but how to govern it transparently enough that customers don't feel manipulated.
ev: MarTech Series · Iterable CMO on AI Engagement

themes.head: Retail Media Measurement and Inflation-Squeezed Spending Force a New ROI Framework
body: ISM's Paul Brenner and IAB's Collin Colburn argue that legacy measurement frameworks were built for a pre-retail-media, pre-AI world and are structurally unable to attribute value across today's fragmented touchpoints. Marketers are being asked to defend budgets using metrics that no longer map to how consumers actually buy.

The mid-year consumer spending report sharpens the urgency: inflation is producing fewer but higher-value orders, compressing the transaction volume that old attribution models relied on. The practical consequence is that AI-assisted measurement — connecting intent signals to incremental sales — is moving from a competitive advantage to a survival requirement for brands in retail-adjacent categories.
ev: Agile Brand · Retail Media Measurement Rules

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — discovery, orchestration, data, trust, and measurement — the marketers who move from AI experimentation to AI infrastructure this quarter will set defaults that are very hard for slower peers to undo.
